hints.content:
We define function $g$ using a definite integral of function $f$. For every $x$-value, we calculate $g(x)$ by taking the definite integral of $f$ from $0$ to $x$.

So to calculate $g(\goldD{3})$ we need to take the definite integral of $f$ from $0$ to $\goldD{3}$:

$g(\goldD{3})=\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\goldD{3}}f(t)\,dt$

This represents the net area between the graph of $f(t)$ and the $x$-axis from $x=0$ to $x=3$.

We can find $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\goldD{3}}f(t)\,dt$ using geometric area formulas.

![The graph of function f has the region between the line segments and x-axis, between x = 0 and x = 3, shaded. The segments at the top of the shaded region start at (0, 5), move downward to (2, 4), move upward and end at (3, 5).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/c4b385f46c4798940527efcf645bab0158e144fd)

We have a $3$ by $5$ rectangle less a triangle with a base of $3$ and a height of $1$, so in total the area is $13.5$.
